chunks: Ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “I wish to perform tamattuʿ with ʿumrah up to hajj, so how should I say it?”

He عليه السلام said: “You say: O Allah, I intend tamattuʿ with ʿumrah up to hajj, upon Your Book and the sunnah (prophetic tradition) of Your Prophet. And if you wish, you may keep within yourself what you intend.”

key_terms.أَضْمَرْتَ: you keep inwardly or internally intend
key_terms.بِٱلْعُمْرَةِ: with ʿumrah, the minor pilgrimage performed before hajj in tamattuʿ
key_terms.عَلَى كِتَابِكَ: in accordance with Your Book, meaning in conformity with divine revelation
key_terms.وَسُنَّةِ نَبِيِّكَ: and the sunnah (prophetic tradition) of Your Prophet, meaning in accordance with the Prophetic way
key_terms.ٱلتَّمَتُّعَ: tamattuʿ, the form of hajj combining ʿumrah with hajj in one journey

ai.seo_question: How should one state the intention for tamattuʿ ʿumrah before hajj according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches the formula for expressing the intention for tamattuʿ in hajj, linking the act to the Book of Allah and the sunnah (prophetic tradition) of His Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم. It also indicates that the pilgrim may keep the intention inwardly, showing flexibility in how niyyah is formulated.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2560 - Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Hammad ibn Uthman, who said:
"I said to Abu Abdullah (as), 'I want to perform Tamattu' with Umrah joined to Hajj. How should I express my intention?'

Imam (as) replied: 'Say: O Allah (swt), I intend to perform Tamattu' with Umrah joined to Hajj, according to Your Book and the Sunnah of Your Prophet. And if you wish, you may internally intend what you want.'"
